accepted.s: The Stand-Up India Scheme was launched on:
accepted.x: Stand-Up India was launched on 5 April 2016.
accepted.tq: Use the direct date-recall approach for a flagship scheme.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the beneficiaries and purpose of the Stand-Up India Scheme?
o: SC/ST and women entrepreneurs aged 18 years or above establishing greenfield enterprises
All unemployed persons establishing government departments
Only existing large companies establishing brownfield enterprises
Only rural artisans receiving grants without enterprise formation
accepted.x: The scheme provides loans to SC/ST and women entrepreneurs aged 18 or above for greenfield enterprises.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the target group from nearby beneficiary categories.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Stand-Up India Scheme, the loan amount generally ranges between:
accepted.x: Stand-Up India loans range from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct range among closely spaced monetary figures.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Stand-Up India Scheme:
1. It is implemented through scheduled commercial bank branches.
2. It covers greenfield enterprises rather than brownfield enterprises.
3. It is confined to manufacturing enterprises.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The scheme operates through scheduled commercial bank branches and supports greenfield enterprises. It covers manufacturing, services, trading and agri-allied activities, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the restrictive sector statement that conflicts with the wider coverage.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A non-individual enterprise seeks assistance under the Stand-Up India Scheme. Which condition would make it eligible in respect of ownership and control?
o: At least 26% shareholding is with a woman or SC/ST person
At least 74% shareholding is with any scheduled bank
The enterprise must be wholly owned by the Central Government
At least 51% shareholding or control is with a woman or SC/ST person
accepted.x: A non-individual enterprise is eligible when at least 51% of its shareholding and control is held by an SC/ST person or a woman.
accepted.tq: Apply the ownership threshold to a non-individual enterprise.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the financial terms of Stand-Up India loans is correct?
o: The loan can cover up to 85% of project cost, with a minimum borrower contribution of 10%.
The loan can cover up to 50% of project cost, with a minimum contribution of 40%.
The scheme provides only grants and has no repayment obligation.
The loan must cover exactly 100% of project cost, without borrower contribution.
accepted.x: Stand-Up India loans may cover up to 85% of project cost, while the borrower contribution is at least 10%.
accepted.tq: Separate project-cost coverage from the borrower-contribution requirement.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The maximum repayment period and moratorium under the Stand-Up India Scheme are respectively:
accepted.x: The repayment period may extend up to seven years and includes an 18-month moratorium.
accepted.tq: Pair the two related numerical conditions correctly.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Stand-Up India implementing ministry—Ministry of Agriculture
Stand-Up India loan period—three years without moratorium
accepted.x: SIDBI provides ₹10,000 crore refinance support. The associated portal is Standupmitra and the nodal ministry is the Ministry of Finance.
accepted.tq: Use the institution-function association to eliminate swapped authorities.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the per-branch norm of Stand-Up India, each bank branch is expected to facilitate at least:
o: One large company and one government enterprise
One SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower
Two SC borrowers and two ST borrowers
One rural artisan and one export-oriented unit
accepted.x: The scheme envisages at least one SC/ST borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch.
accepted.tq: Recall the scheme’s distinctive per-branch numerical norm.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As specified for the 15th Finance Commission period, the operational period of Stand-Up India extended up to:
accepted.x: The scheme was operational up to 31 March 2025 during the 15th Finance Commission period.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely spaced scheme-end dates.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Up to 31 March 2025, Stand-Up India had sanctioned approximately:
accepted.x: The scheme had covered about 2.75 lakh loans amounting to ₹62,790 crore by 31 March 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the loan count with its corresponding aggregate amount.
accepted.sec: Stand-Up India - target groups, loan range, greenfield, per branch norm  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which institution is the nodal agency for recognition of start-ups under the Startup India framework?
accepted.x: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) is the nodal agency for Startup India recognition.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct institutional authority rather than a financing agency.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Startup India framework:
1. Its Action Plan contains 19 points.
2. An entity formed by splitting or reconstructing an existing business is not treated as a start-up.
3. A start-up may be constituted only as a private limited company.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Action Plan has 19 points, and an entity formed by splitting or reconstructing an existing business is excluded. Eligible legal forms also include partnerships, LLPs and cooperatives, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the word ‘only’ when the legal-form coverage is broader.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares an ordinary start-up with a deep-tech start-up?
o: Ordinary start-up: up to 20 years and ₹300 crore turnover; deep-tech start-up: up to 10 years and ₹200 crore turnover
Ordinary start-up: up to 10 years and ₹200 crore turnover; deep-tech start-up: up to 20 years and ₹300 crore turnover
Both: up to 10 years and ₹300 crore turnover
Both: up to 20 years and ₹200 crore turnover
accepted.x: The stated criteria are up to 10 years and turnover not above ₹200 crore for a start-up, and up to 20 years and ₹300 crore for a deep-tech start-up. Both may have the listed legal forms.
accepted.tq: Read both age and turnover columns before selecting the comparison.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated benefit available under the Startup India framework?
o: Self-certification under specified labour and environmental laws
Permanent exemption from all taxes for the entire life of the enterprise
Income-tax deduction for three consecutive years out of ten under Section 80-IAC
accepted.x: The framework provides a tax deduction for three consecutive years out of ten, self-certification and fast-track patent facilities. It does not provide a permanent exemption from all taxes.
accepted.tq: Find the exaggerated benefit using the extreme-word trap.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: For eligibility under Section 80-IAC, the relevant start-up incorporation condition stated for the framework is incorporation before:
accepted.x: The stated incorporation cut-off for the Section 80-IAC benefit is before 1 April 2030.
accepted.tq: Recall the cut-off date independently of the duration of the deduction.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Startup Advisory Council was notified in:
accepted.x: The National Startup Advisory Council was notified in January 2020, specifically on 22 January 2020.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the council’s notification date from the Startup India launch date.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Startup India Yatra primarily seeks entrepreneurial talent in:
accepted.x: Startup India Yatra searches for entrepreneurial talent in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
accepted.tq: Use the geographical target as the distinguishing feature.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme:
1. It has an outlay of ₹945 crore.
2. It was launched on 19 April 2021.
3. It provides support only through direct loans from commercial banks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: SISFS has an outlay of ₹945 crore and was launched on 19 April 2021. Support is routed through incubators, not only through direct commercial-bank loans.
accepted.tq: Identify the intermediary institution in a scheme-delivery statement.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme, the maximum support specified for proof of concept and investment is respectively:
accepted.x: SISFS provides up to ₹20 lakh as a grant for proof of concept and up to ₹50 lakh as investment. It operates through incubators, each of which may receive up to ₹5 crore.
accepted.tq: Match the two support ceilings with their respective purposes.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Fund of Funds for Startups?
o: It is managed by NCGTC and gives only collateral-free loans directly to borrowers.
It is managed by SIDBI and invests through SEBI-registered AIFs rather than directly in start-ups.
It is managed by NITI Aayog and provides grants only for prototypes.
It is managed by DPIIT and invests only in government companies.
accepted.x: The ₹10,000 crore Fund of Funds is managed by SIDBI and invests through SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds; it does not invest directly in start-ups.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘not directly’ distinction in an institutional-function question.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Fund of Funds 2.0 is intended to provide an additional corpus mainly for:
o: Deep technology, space and artificial intelligence
Traditional handicrafts, tourism and fisheries only
Public distribution and food processing only
accepted.x: Fund of Funds 2.0 provides another ₹10,000 crore aimed at deep tech, space and artificial intelligence.
accepted.tq: Link the second fund version with its specified priority sectors.
accepted.sec: Start-up India - definition, DPIIT recognition, NSAC, Yatra, Seed Fund, Fund of Funds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Udyam Abhilasha is a national entrepreneurship-awareness campaign associated with SIDBI. Swavalambini is associated with MSDE and NITI Aayog, while ASPIRE and PM Vishwakarma are Ministry of MSME programmes.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure programme-agency pair and eliminate swapped ministries.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship programmes → objective and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Swavalambini is primarily associated with:
accepted.x: Swavalambini is a women’s entrepreneurship programme in the North-East, implemented by MSDE with NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Separate programme beneficiaries from programme-delivery institutions.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship programmes → objective and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. PM Vishwakarma — Traditional artisans in 18 trades
2. ASPIRE — Livelihood Business Incubators in the agro-rural sector
3. Udyam Abhilasha — National-level entrepreneurship awareness campaign
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. PM Vishwakarma supports traditional artisans, ASPIRE promotes agro-rural incubators, and Udyam Abhilasha promotes entrepreneurship awareness.
accepted.tq: Check each programme against its stated objective before using the all-correct option.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship programmes → objective and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with PM Vishwakarma?
o: Loans up to ₹20 crore and a guarantee fee of 1%
Loans up to ₹3 lakh, a toolkit incentive of ₹15,000 and a stipend of ₹500 per day
A grant of ₹20 lakh for proof of concept through incubators
An equity investment of ₹50 lakh through AIFs
accepted.x: PM Vishwakarma, launched in September 2023 under the Ministry of MSME, provides loans up to ₹3 lakh, a ₹15,000 toolkit incentive and a ₹500-per-day stipend.
accepted.tq: Match multiple benefit figures to the correct programme.
accepted.sec: Entrepreneurship programmes → objective and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: RKVY-RAFTAAR agribusiness incubation support provides up to which amounts at the idea/pre-seed and seed stages respectively?
accepted.x: RKVY-RAFTAAR provides up to ₹5 lakh at the idea/pre-seed stage and ₹25 lakh at the seed stage.
accepted.tq: Pair stage-wise financial ceilings in their correct order.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about support for agri-start-ups is correct?
1. ₹146.16 crore was provided for 1,943 agri-start-ups during FY 2020–25.
2. MANAGE, Hyderabad is among the Knowledge Partners involved in selection and incubation.
3. Support is restricted to the post-listing stage of agri-companies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The stated support was ₹146.16 crore for 1,943 agri-start-ups during FY 2020–25, with Knowledge Partners such as MANAGE, Hyderabad involved in selection and incubation. It is not restricted to post-listing companies.
accepted.tq: Reject the false stage restriction and retain the two specific factual statements.
accepted.sec: Start-up ecosystem institutions - agri-startups, AIM, NIDHI, GII rank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Atal Innovation Mission is associated with which institution and year of establishment?
accepted.x: Atal Innovation Mission was established under NITI Aayog in 2016 and includes Atal Tinkering Labs and incubators.
accepted.tq: Combine the sponsoring institution with the establishment year.
accepted.sec: Start-up ecosystem institutions - agri-startups, AIM, NIDHI, GII rank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: AIM 2.0, approved in 2024, is stated to continue up to March 2028 with an outlay of ₹2,750 crore and:
accepted.x: AIM 2.0 continues up to March 2028, with ₹2,750 crore and 2,500 new Atal Tinkering Labs.
accepted.tq: Match the programme’s duration, outlay and physical target.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with NIDHI?
o: PRAYAS—prototype development; EIR—fellowship up to ₹30,000 per month
accepted.x: NIDHI is a DST umbrella programme for converting knowledge-based innovations into start-ups. PRAYAS supports prototypes, while the EIR programme offers a fellowship of up to ₹30,000 per month.
accepted.tq: Match each named NIDHI component with its specific function.

accepted.s: India’s rank in the Global Innovation Index 2025 was:
accepted.x: India ranked 38th in the Global Innovation Index 2025.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact rank while rejecting nearby numerical distractors.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes venture capital?
o: Early-stage equity investment accompanied by active guidance for high-growth firms
Collateral-free bank lending guaranteed through NCGTC
Individuals investing their own money at the idea or seed stage
Small sums collected from many people through online platforms
accepted.x: Venture capital consists of early-stage equity investment with active guidance for high-growth firms. The other descriptions refer to crowdfunding, angel investment and CGSS respectively.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among similar start-up financing sources by their defining features.
accepted.sec: Start-up financing sources - angel, VC, crowdfunding, credit guarantee  [other exams]

accepted.s: An online platform collects small contributions from a large number of individuals to finance a new enterprise. This is an example of:
accepted.x: Crowdfunding raises small sums from many people through online platforms.
accepted.tq: Apply the financing-source definition to a practical situation.
accepted.sec: Start-up financing sources - angel, VC, crowdfunding, credit guarantee  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS):
1. It was introduced in October 2022.
2. It facilitates collateral-free loans through a guarantee provided by NCGTC.
3. The maximum guarantee-supported amount is ₹20 crore per borrower.
4. The fee is 1% for champion sectors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: CGSS was introduced in October 2022, uses NCGTC guarantees for collateral-free loans, has a ₹20 crore maximum per borrower and charges a 1% fee for champion sectors.
accepted.tq: Verify each quantitative and institutional detail before selecting all the correct statements.
accepted.sec: Start-up financing sources - angel, VC, crowdfunding, credit guarantee  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding start-up taxation and financing?
o: The Fund of Funds invests directly in every recognised start-up.
Angel tax was abolished only for government investors.
CGSS provides only grants and not guaranteed loans.
Angel tax was abolished for all investors in Budget 2024–25.
accepted.x: Angel tax was abolished for all investors in Budget 2024–25. The Fund of Funds invests through SEBI-registered AIFs, while CGSS supports collateral-free loans through guarantees.
accepted.tq: Separate a broad tax-policy change from the mechanisms of funding schemes.
accepted.sec: Start-up financing sources - angel, VC, crowdfunding, credit guarantee  [other exams]

accepted.s: The States’ Startup Ranking Framework of DPIIT primarily promotes:
o: Allocation of all start-up funds exclusively to one state
Direct ranking of individual start-up founders by personal income
Competitive federalism by assessing state start-up policies and their implementation
Assessment of only the number of unicorns in each district
accepted.x: The framework promotes competitive federalism by assessing the policies adopted by states and their implementation for start-up development.
accepted.tq: Identify the framework’s purpose rather than a narrow output indicator.
accepted.sec: States' Start-up Ranking - categories, AP position

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a category under the States’ Startup Ranking Framework?
accepted.x: The categories include Best Performers, Top Performers, Leaders, Aspiring Leaders and Emerging Start-up Ecosystems. Global Innovation Champions is not one of the listed categories.
accepted.tq: Find the category that does not belong to the official classification.
accepted.sec: States' Start-up Ranking - categories, AP position

accepted.s: According to the stated States’ Startup Ranking 2022 and India Innovation Index 2022 positions, Andhra Pradesh was:
o: No. 1 in the States’ Startup Ranking and 9th in the India Innovation Index
9th in the States’ Startup Ranking and No. 1 in the India Innovation Index
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh was ranked No. 1 in the States’ Startup Ranking 2022 and 9th in the India Innovation Index 2022.
accepted.tq: Keep the two rankings separate and avoid reversing their positions.
accepted.sec: States' Start-up Ranking - categories, AP position

accepted.s: A privately held start-up valued at US$1 billion or more before listing is commonly called a:
accepted.x: A unicorn is a privately held start-up valued at US$1 billion or more before it is listed.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise valuation and ownership definition of a unicorn.
accepted.sec: Unicorns - India's global rank, number

accepted.s: According to the government count stated for January 2026, India had approximately how many active unicorns, with what combined value?
accepted.x: The government count was approximately 125 active unicorns with a combined value of $389 billion. The count was only four in 2014.
accepted.tq: Match the count and aggregate valuation rather than selecting either figure alone.
accepted.sec: Unicorns - India's global rank, number

accepted.s: Which country-wise statement is correct according to the Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2026 figures stated?
o: India ranked fourth with 61 unicorns, while the UK had 70.
India ranked fourth with 381 unicorns, while China had 61.
India ranked second with 806 unicorns, while the USA had 70.
India ranked third with 70 unicorns, while the UK had 61.
accepted.x: India ranked fourth with 61 unicorns, down from 64, and was overtaken by the UK with 70. The USA had 806 and China 381.
accepted.tq: Compare rank and country counts without confusing the different country totals.
accepted.sec: Unicorns - India's global rank, number

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the stated city-wise distribution of unicorns in India under the Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2026?
accepted.x: The stated city-wise figures are 25 unicorns for Bengaluru and 13 for Mumbai.
accepted.tq: Match each city with its own count instead of reversing the pair.
accepted.sec: Unicorns - India's global rank, number

accepted.s: The difference between the government count of active Indian unicorns and the Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2026 count is best explained by:
o: The conversion of every unicorn into a listed company
The exclusion of all privately held firms from the government count
A constitutional change in the definition of a start-up
accepted.x: The figures differ because the government and Hurun use different methodologies for counting unicorns.
accepted.tq: Identify methodology as the explanation for apparently conflicting statistics.
accepted.sec: Unicorns - India's global rank, number
